target_customer: Insurers, MGAs and carriers that outsource claims handling to a third party administrator
problem: Traditional TPAs are slow, error prone and damage customer trust, and insurers lack tech-enabled claims outsourcing.
business_model: Service fees as a tech-enabled third party administrator for insurance claims

founders.name: Pavel Gertsberg
previous_startups: Fluffy (pet insurance, per YC page; Atomico note says it was acquired by Zurich Insurance)
founders.background_notes: YC page: head of growth at SaaS and InsurTech companies before Fluffy, which reached over 20,000 customers.

founders.name: German Mikulski
founders.background_notes: YC page: automated about 70% of Fluffy back office with AI and built systems at Deutsche Bank processing over $100M.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly workflow software and LLM tooling plus human adjusters; the hard parts are operational and licensing rather than technical.

defensibility.rationale: TPA relationships with insurers are sticky and Lloyd's delegated authority is a credential, but services can be copied by funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The tech.eu article says the market is dominated by large services companies; no dated evidence of incumbents copying the model was found.

market_need_then: The founders ran an insurer and found third party claims agencies unreliable, with tech.eu citing nearly 20% of TPA payouts as incorrect.

branding.name_origin: The company's site plays on sorted as resolved, contrasting a claim that is closed with one that is sorted.

identity.visual_style: Real life photography of mishaps and team portraits, clean spacious layouts
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, warm and confident with wordplay

branding.brand_signature: ClosedSorted: closed versus truly sorted claims

brand_strength.rationale: Name and messaging are distinctive and tied to the value proposition, but no source shows community or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: ClaimSorted is active, raising a $3M pre-seed in October 2024 and a $13.3M seed in October 2025 led by Atomico, with founders who previously ran an insurer. The team wedge is operational: pairing AI with human claims specialists as a TPA, with claimed partnerships including Lloyd's delegated authority.
notes: The Claims Journal piece is sponsored content, so traction numbers are company claims. A dated competitor search found no sources from around mid 2024 naming direct AI TPA rivals (Corgi and software vendors surfaced but undated or later), so the list is empty. CB Insights total of $16.3M is consistent with the two rounds. Atomico note says Fluffy was acquired by Zurich; I could not open that page (429) so it comes from a search snippet.
